claims.text: Coherently embedded L12-ordered precipitates can be formed within an fcc high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Introducing coherent L12 precipitates into an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix will increase coercivity above 100 Oe.
The proposed L12 precipitates will be rich in Ti and Ni and Ni3Ti-like.
Strain from coherent precipitates will locally suppress orbital-moment quenching.
The precipitate-containing alloy will retain a magnetic ordering temperature significantly above room temperature.
A single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has low coercivity because its orbital moments are suppressed.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a paramagnetic or weakly ferromagnetic state in the single-phase Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
Annealing at 900–950 °C followed by controlled cooling will precipitate coherent nanoscale L12 particles in the fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The fcc matrix will remain stable over the proposed 300–600 K operating interval.
Coherent L12 precipitates will pin magnetic domain walls.
Coherent L12 precipitates will generate local lattice strain that modifies the electronic density of states at Fe/Co/Ni interfaces.
Local strain and chemical ordering will break the symmetry responsible for orbital-moment quenching in the single-phase fcc alloy.
The strain-induced electronic modification will increase the spin-orbit-coupling contribution to magnetic anisotropy energy.
Increased magnetic anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will raise the coercive field.
The composite alloy will have a Curie temperature above 400 K.
Coercivity will scale with the volume fraction and coherency of the L12 precipitates.
A precipitate-free single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti baseline will have coercivity below 50 Oe.
Transformation of the coherent L12 precipitates into incoherent Heusler or BCC phases would alter magnetic coupling or reduce the Curie temperature.
